provenance.reviewers: 4 read-only reviewer subagents (correctness, security, tests, ticket-fit) on Sonnet + SonarCloud via CI

findings.title: Owner deleted between page query and graph fetch answers 500
findings.observation: a concurrent delete after the page SELECT leaves an id the graph fetch cannot find, and the request fails.
findings.why: design.md decided to surface it, never silently drop a selected owner.

findings.title: Page, count and graph fetch share no snapshot
findings.observation: a write between the count and the page query can make totalElements disagree with content.
findings.why: design.md Risks accepts offset drift under concurrent writes; snapshots are out of scope.

findings.title: Empty table chrome shows before the first page arrives
findings.observation: headers render with no rows while the first request is in flight.
findings.why: marked aria-busy and claims nothing; no false "no owners" message.

findings.title: HttpParams sends "+" raw, read as a space
findings.observation: a prefix like O+Brien would be decoded by the server as "O Brien".
findings.why: refuted — Angular 16 encodes '+'; owner.service.spec.ts:80 decodes it back verbatim.

findings.title: lastName has no length cap
findings.observation: a multi-KB prefix goes into the LIKE parameter unbounded.
findings.why: pre-existing filter, bound as a parameter; Tomcat caps the request line.

findings.title: Name column shows "First Last" but sorts by last name
findings.observation: rows read as unsorted to a user scanning first names; tests only mirror the SQL order.
findings.why: Q3 decided by the human: Name sorts by last name, first name, id.

findings.title: Index test never checks the planner uses the indexes
findings.observation: only the DDL is asserted; a seq scan would leave every test green.
findings.why: plans need 100k rows; that measurement is deferred by the spec.

findings.title: Query-budget test is @Transactional, may mask lazy loads
findings.observation: one session spans the request, unlike production, so a missed association might go unnoticed.
findings.why: refuted — statistics count every prepared statement, lazy loads included; a miss exceeds 3.

findings.title: OwnerTest.getAll narrowed to lastName=Franklin
findings.observation: the unfiltered default page is no longer requested there.
findings.why: refuted — OwnerListTest.java:47 pins the unfiltered default page against SQL.

findings.title: No recovery when the current page falls past the last
findings.observation: owners deleted elsewhere leave an empty page with a nonzero total.
findings.why: the spec asks only that navigation stays; its component test covers it.

findings.title: sort.direction || 'asc' hides a cleared sort
findings.observation: if clearing ever fired, the grid would load ascending while the header shows no arrow.
findings.why: matSortDisableClear prevents it; the bound matSortDirection redraws the arrow anyway.

findings.title: V4 indexes nobody asked for
findings.observation: three indexes add write overhead on owners, unmeasured.
findings.why: design.md Decision 3 and task 2.1 specify them.

findings.title: Add Owner shown during load and after errors
findings.observation: the old isOwnersDataReceived gate is gone.
findings.why: the spec requires Add Owner across loading, empty and error layouts.

autofixes.title: A failed page hid the paginator, so only a new search could retry
autofixes.observation: on error the component set loaded=false, which hid the paginator with the table. A transient 500 on page 3 could be retried only through Find Owner, which restarts from page 0.
autofixes.fix: keep the last good total on failure so the paginator stays; noMatches now also requires no error.

autofixes.title: Paging step waited for rows to change, which a page may not do
autofixes.observation: the step polled until the listed ids differed. A sort or size change that leaves the first page's ids unchanged would time out after 10 s.
autofixes.fix: wait for the /api/owners response, then for the table's aria-busy to turn false.

autofixes.title: Rejected request values echoed into the log and the 400 body
autofixes.observation: ?page=x%0d%0a… and ?sort=… were copied into log.warn and the ProblemDetail. A caller could forge log lines and have arbitrary text reflected back.
autofixes.fix: name the parameter and the expected type or values, never the raw value.

autofixes.title: Validation literals duplicated four times in the advice
autofixes.observation: the new type-mismatch handler made "Validation failed: {}" and "Validation Error" the fourth copy of each.

autofixes.title: Size assertions on .length instead of toHaveSize
autofixes.observation: eleven expect(x.length).toBe(n) report a bare number on failure, not the collection.

autofixes.title: Injected services not readonly
autofixes.observation: the router and the owner service are never reassigned.

assumptions.title: An empty ?size=, ?page= or ?sort= means omitted, not malformed
assumptions.why: Spring's defaultValue also covers an empty string, and the spec defines only the omitted case. Pulling it down: the spec says malformed input is a 400, and size= could be read as malformed.

assumptions.title: A type mismatch is a 400 on every endpoint, not only the list
assumptions.alternative: scope the 400 to listOwners, leave /api/owners/abc a 500
assumptions.why: a 500 for bad client input is wrong everywhere, and the advice is global by design. Pulling it down: the spec promises the detail and CRUD contracts unchanged, and /api/owners/abc moved from 500 to 400.

assumptions.title: A page whose offset overflows an int is a 400
assumptions.alternative: clamp it and answer an empty page
assumptions.why: the spec names "unrepresentable" page numbers as a 400, and Hibernate's offset is an int. Only how far "unrepresentable" reaches was mine to choose.

assumptions.title: Sort keys and directions are case-sensitive
assumptions.why: the spec lists exactly four lowercase tokens and rejects everything else. A lenient parser would be friendlier to hand-written URLs, but nothing in-repo writes them.

assumptions.title: The error view shows the server's message verbatim
assumptions.alternative: a generic "could not load owners", details only in the console
assumptions.why: the spec asks only for an explicit error. The handler's text ("server returned code 500…") helps whoever reports it, but it is technical wording on a clinic screen.

assumptions.title: No-match message keeps the old "LastName" wording
assumptions.why: the spec only adds the submitted prefix, and e2e text matches may rely on the old wording.
